newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: PM SAYS COUNTRY TO BECOME INVESTOR FRIENDLY.
newsitem.headline: PM SAYS COUNTRY TO BECOME INVESTOR FRIENDLY.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that his government was determined to improve the country's investment and business climate.
"Lithuania's economy will become absolutely open to international trade," Vagnorius told a group of investors, diplomats and government officials gathered for an investors forum.
"We are determined to eliminate all obstacles to business," he said, adding that his administration was ready to intervene directly to help investors sort out problems with civil servants.
Foreign investment is a key area where Lithuania is viewed as lagging behind Baltic siblings Estonia and Latvia.
A recent survey of foreign businesses polled by the Lithuanian Invtesment Agency found widespread dissatisfaction with the legal, tax and customs systems.
Vagnorius said that his government would simplify the tax and legal systems, make them investor-firendly, and root out corruption.
"We are determined to take concrete steps to simplify the tax system," Vagnorius said.
"We have launched a sever fight against smuggling and organised crime," he added.
